text.title: Junior Next Pr Checklist Template Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete checklist derived from a nine-comment review of a billing-API PR (four items, one blocker, one deferred, one retired, one routed to mypy), the Markdown the junior pastes, a note on every non-obvious value, and one bad checklist showing what the validator and the mentor reject.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: Marek reviewed Priya's PR #412 on the billing API and left nine comments: a missing transaction around two writes, a PR description with no ticket link, three nullable parameters without guards, missing docstrings, `print` in the payment path, and three formatting nits. Priya's previous checklist (from PR #398) had four items; two were ticked on #398 and again on #412, one was ticked once, one was new.

example.title: Priya's checklist for the PR after #412
example.note: Nine comments became four items and one deferred entry: the three formatting nits never became candidates because `ruff format` already owns them, and the `print` comment is parked in `deferred` with its permalink until an item retires (r-three-to-seven-items, r-machine-checkable-items-become-lint).

`c1` is the single blocker because ADR-014 makes transactional boundaries a written standard and the missing transaction is the only comment that would fail a review on its own; `c4` (docstrings) has no written standard, so it is `preference:@marek` and can only be `should` (r-severity-ordered-one-blocker, r-item-cites-team-standard).

`c3` can be enforced by `mypy --strict-optional`; the ticket that turns it on in CI is #419, and `prs_since_automation_landed` is 0 because it has not landed yet. Once it does, the item survives one more PR and is dropped (r-machine-checkable-items-become-lint).

`c2` was on the #398 checklist and ticked only once, so it carries with `carried_count = 1`; the test-file naming item was ticked on #398 and #412, so it is in `retired`. No item reached three carries, so `pairing_sessions` is empty (r-carry-forward-and-retire).

Every `ticked_by_junior` is false because the checklist has not been pasted into the next PR yet; the ticks are Priya's to make, and `posting` records that Marek only verifies (r-junior-self-ticks-before-review).
`review.status` is `ready_for_mentor_review`: Marek confirms the four permalinks and the blocker label, dates the confirmation, and hands the list to Priya himself (human checkpoint).

example.title: The Markdown Priya pastes into her next PR description
example.code:
## Next-PR checklist (from #412, confirmed by @marek 2026-06-19)
- [ ] **blocking** c1 — Every new database write runs inside a transaction or the PR description says why it does not (ADR-014) — [origin](https://github.com/acme/billing-api/pull/412#discussion_r1893320011) - [ ] should c2 (carried x1) — The PR description links the ticket and lists the manual test that was run (CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-description) — [origin](https://github.com/acme/billing-api/pull/412#issuecomment-2210377) - [ ] should c3 — Every nullable parameter has an explicit guard or a `?` type annotation (style-guide#nullability; mypy --strict-optional lands via #419) — [origin](https://github.com/acme/billing-api/pull/412#discussion_r1893321440) - [ ] should c4 — Every new public function has a docstring stating its return type and raised exceptions (preference:@marek) — [origin](https://github.com/acme/billing-api/pull/412#discussion_r1893322905)
Retired: test-file naming (ticked on #398 and #412). Deferred: structured logger in the payment path.
example.note: One screen, severity first, permalinks on every line, the retired and deferred items visible so progress is legible. Priya ticks before requesting review; an unticked paste is sent back before code is read.

example.title: What the validator and the mentor reject
example.note: Validator output: `$.items: 2 items, minItems=3`, `$.items[0].check: 'Be more careful with null handling and think about edge cases' does not match pattern ...`, `$.items[0].carried_count: 4 violates maximum=2`, `$.items[0].severity: must equal 'should', got 'blocking'`, `$.items[1].lint.rule: missing required field`, `$.items[1].lint.automation_ticket: missing required field`, `$.blocking_item_count: 2 violates maximum=1`, `$.posting.junior_pastes_into_next_pr_description: must equal True, got False`, `$.posting.ticks_authored_by: must equal 'junior', got 'mentor'`, `$.posting.mentor_verifies_only: must equal True, got False`, `$.review.handed_to_junior_by_agent: must equal False, got True`, `$.review.mentor_confirmed_permalinks_and_severity_on: missing required field`.

What the mentor sees beyond the validator: the fourth carry of "be more careful" is the item that should have become a pairing session two PRs ago (r-carry-forward-and-retire); import order and whitespace are a formatter's job and never belonged on a human checklist (r-machine-checkable-items-become-lint); the `print` and transaction comments, the two that mattered, are not on the list at all (r-item-traces-to-review-comment).
